methods.description: Check consecutive differences, or read the change per position from the nth-term linear rule.
Use a+(n-1)d to simplify the rule or evaluate a requested term, retaining exact surds where supplied.
Set the requested term value equal to a+(n-1)d and solve for its positive integer position, including finite length.
Solve the term inequality, select the first valid positive integer position and evaluate its term.
Write specified individual terms using a+(n-1)d, then subtract simultaneous equations to find a and d; adding two individual terms is not the partial-sum formula.
Set consecutive differences equal to find the parameter, then apply the nth-term formula.
Use the logarithm quotient law for consecutive differences, then substitute the exact common difference into the AP rule.
